requirements.note: Inset-grouped Lists screen with Today/All smart rows and My Lists; each has an open count (Today 25, All 135) and a coloured list icon. Counts update after adding, completing and deleting.
Open tasks are listed first, then a 'Completed 7' header that starts collapsed and expands on tap. Tapping the checkbox moves a task to Completed with an animation, and the count updates.

The New Task sheet has a title, notes, a list picker, a Due Date switch with an inline graphical calendar, and a None/Low/High segmented control. Tapping a row opens Details for editing; the edited title was saved.
Overdue dates are red with an exclamation-circle icon and the word 'Overdue'. High priority shows an orange '!!!' and low shows '!'.
Swipe-to-delete works. Reordering works only after More > Reorder Tasks (edit mode with reorder handles); the new order survived a relaunch.
Add List opens an alert with a text field; rename and delete are in the list's More menu, and delete asks for confirmation. Also has a nice empty state for a new list ('No Tasks').
After relaunch, the added, completed, deleted and reordered tasks were all kept.

tells: Reordering is hidden behind More > Reorder Tasks rather than being available by long-pressing a row.
The rename alert does not preselect the existing name; typed text is appended to it.
The Completed header's disclosure glyph is small and sits next to the count, a little unlike a system section header.
The New Task sheet does not scroll its fields above the keyboard; the date and priority controls stay hidden until you drag the form.
A.scroll: The 135-row All list scrolls smoothly and decelerates naturally. Rows were already drawn mid-fling with no blanks or pop-in, the large title collapses into the inline title, and pulling past the top rubber-bands.

requirements.note: Inset-grouped Lists screen with Today/All rows (icons) and My Lists with open counts; the counts update correctly. User lists have no icons or colours.
Open tasks are listed first, then a 'Completed (7)' row that starts expanded and collapses with a chevron. The checkbox completes and reopens tasks, and counts update.
The New Task sheet has a title, list menu, Due Date switch with a compact date picker, a Priority pop-up menu and notes. Tapping a task opens Details; the edits saved.
Overdue tasks show the date in red with 'Overdue ·'. High priority shows a red '!!!' and low a grey '!'.
Every row has a visible drag handle and dragging reorders straight away; the order persisted. Swipe left shows a red Delete action.
The + button opens a New List sheet. Touching and holding a list gives a context menu with Rename and Delete, swiping a list deletes it, and delete is confirmed by an alert.
After relaunch, the completion, the added task, the deletion and the reorder were all kept.

bugs: After scrolling the All list down and flinging back to the top, the first four rows are drawn without separators; the gap remains once the list has settled.
tells: A footer under My Lists says 'Swipe a list to delete it; touch and hold to rename it.' Native apps don't explain their gestures in body text.
Drag handles show on every row all the time, not only in edit mode.
Row layout is inconsistent: notes sometimes sit on the same line after the date or list name, and sometimes wrap to their own line, so the rows look like flowed inline text.
Task lists use a plain style with a separator line above the first row, while the main and form screens are inset-grouped.
User lists have no icons or colours, which makes the main screen sparse next to the Today/All rows.
Dates switch between relative weekday names ('Tuesday', 'Saturday') and absolute dates.
B.scroll: The All list scrolls and flings smoothly with no blank rows, and the large title collapses properly. Separators disappear from the top rows after scrolling back, which looks unpolished.

why: Both apps meet every requirement and persist reliably. A looks and behaves more like Reminders: inset-grouped task cards, coloured list icons, date and overdue glyphs, coloured list tags in Today/All, a collapsed Completed section, and a proper empty state. B's always-on drag handles, gesture-instruction footer, inconsistent inline row layout and missing separators after scrolling make it feel less hand-built.
